name: runway-mcp
description: A memory for your job hunt: which jobs you applied to, what state each is in, and which resume version you sent — plus a live work-authorization warning.
long_description:
runwayMCP remembers your job hunt so you don't have to. Paste a job description into the conversation — the server never fetches it — and Claude extracts the title, company, and country; runwayMCP persists the record, your application status across 7 states, and every tailored resume version you send, linked to the job it was written for.

**The headline query:** "did I apply to Datadog?" → `list_jobs(company="Datadog")` → "yes, and here's the exact resume you sent" (`get_job` → linked resume versions → `get_resume_version`).

**What it does in one call (`analyze_job`):**
- Loads your general resume text so Claude can score the fit against the pasted posting (0–100)
- Compares the job's country against the countries you've declared you may legally work in, and warns on a mismatch — computed live, never cached
- Returns a scoring rubric Claude applies to produce an `APPLY / CONSIDER / SKIP` recommendation

**Setup:** Tell Claude to save your resume (`save_resume_version`) and declare where you may legally work (`set_work_authorization`) — both are one-time steps before the first `analyze_job` call.

**Storage:** A single local SQLite database. Upgrading from a pre-0.3.0 install migrates your existing `jobs.json`/`resumes.json` automatically and backs up the originals — no action needed.

**How it works:** The tools persist and shape data; Claude drafts and tailors your resume text, scores the fit, and decides what to save. No MCP sampling is used, so it works on any host.

tools.name: analyze_job
tools.description: Loads your general resume and a scoring guide for a job you are evaluating. Claude scores the match against the job posting text in the conversation and applies the APPLY/CONSIDER/SKIP rules; the server does not fetch postings or score.

tools.name: save_resume_version
tools.description: Save a new resume version (raw text). The first save with parent_id=None establishes your general resume; later saves can tailor it for a specific job via parent_id and job_id — job_id must reference a job already saved with save_job_analysis, so call that first.

tools.name: get_resume_version
tools.description: Retrieve a resume version by id, or the most recently saved one via id="latest".

tools.name: list_resume_versions
tools.description: List saved resume versions (newest first), optionally filtered by job_id. Returns summaries, not full text.

tools.name: save_job_analysis
tools.description: Persist an analyzed job's title, company, country, score, and recommendation, plus the full pasted job description (jd_text). Requires a url and/or a custom_title (the handle used to find this record again). Upserts by id, then by url.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Retrieve a single stored job by id, url, or custom_title, with linked resume version summaries. include_description=True also returns the full pasted job description.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: List stored job records, optionally filtered by company (substring match), application status (one value or a list), minimum score, or date, sorted and limited.

tools.name: set_application_status
tools.description: Set a stored job's application status (not_applied, applied, interviewing, offer, rejected, withdrawn, ghosted). Any status can transition to any other.

tools.name: delete_job
tools.description: Permanently delete a stored job by id or url. For a record that should not exist (mistyped, duplicate, test data) — not the same as the 'withdrawn' status, which is a real event worth keeping. The captured job description goes with it; tailored resume versions are kept and only unlinked (job_id set to NULL). No undo: the result names the job and every version that was unlinked.

tools.name: set_work_authorization
tools.description: Declare the full list of countries you may legally work in (replaces any prior declaration). Required before analyze_job will run: it compares each job's country against this list live and warns on a mismatch, but never blocks or stores the result.
